purpose: Durable rotation registry for recovered and active long-form Warhammer 40K chronicles. Recovery backlog takes priority over new continuation work. Once recovered material is indexed and verified, rotate between distinct existing story lines rather than repeatedly extending one arc.

policy.chapterCapRule: Hard cap of 40 chapters per book. A continuing story that reaches Chapter XL must close that book at or before Chapter XL; further narrative continues as a subsequent book rather than Chapter XLI.

active.title: The Long Patrol of Broussard
active.sourceDocument: The Long Patrol of Broussard — Working Draft
active.recoveredThrough: X. THE FORWARD HOLDS — complete through Broussard organizing the search for Jerrik Noll, Edren Vale and Pallas Dorn and ending: “Let’s go find them.”
active.sourceObservedThrough: X. THE FORWARD HOLDS — complete; the connected Google working draft contains no later chapter.
active.currentEndpoint: XIII. THE THING UNDER THE ICE — a large High Presidio predator breaches the recovery perimeter and attacks Chimera Two before moving beneath the stranded Hesperant Vale. Broussard uses the four Chimeras as a controlled fire channel, refuses pursuit onto fractured ice, releases the recovery hauler from its tow rig before the predator can use the connection against the ship, and kills the animal when it resurfaces. Chimera Two remains mobile with a destroyed vision block and minor track damage; no additional personnel are lost. The predator takes much of the tow alignment into the broken ice, and the ship repair estimate slips to roughly thirty-seven hours. The fourteen-second telemetry anomaly remains untouched and separate from the predator attack and prior electrocution.
active.nextSlice: When Broussard next becomes rotation-eligible, advance the recovery after the predator attack toward restored mobility and eventual convoy return. Preserve the damaged-but-mobile Chimera Two, lost/delayed tow alignment, contracted perimeter, roughly thirty-seven-hour repair estimate, genuine electrocution accident, and unresolved fourteen-second telemetry gap. The deeper falsified-origin/Genestealer truth remains concealed until earned; do not make the predator attack explain it. Apply human-conversation governance and preserve the outcome lock that Broussard ultimately escorts the repaired freighter back to the convoy while the reader eventually sees the hidden Xenos compromise survive. The book may contain no more than 40 chapters.
constraints: Fourteen-second telemetry gap is a surface anomaly, not the main plot hole.
Deep-indexed older telemetry was falsified to conceal the freighter's true port of origin.
Hesperant Vale crew is secretly compromised by Genestealer influence.
Genestealer hybrids are hidden among loose produce bins in the forward holds.
Broussard's detachment successfully returns the damaged freighter to the convoy after fighting additional High Presidio predators.
The reader sees the hidden Xenos travesty continuing beneath the apparent successful rescue.
Recover Google source sequentially and verbatim before fresh expansion.
Jerrik Noll, Edren Vale and Pallas Dorn died by accidental electrocution at an intermittent damaged service-junction cross-feed.
Jerrik was the first casualty; Edren and Pallas died in sequence while trying to help the man ahead of them.
The electrocution is a genuine mundane accident inside the larger mystery and must not be retroactively rewritten as a Genestealer kill.
Broussard still remembers the unexplained telemetry discrepancy after the bodies are recovered.
Hard cap: no book may exceed 40 chapters; Chapter XL is the latest permissible chapter number within a book.

characterContinuityAssessment.segment: XIII. THE THING UNDER THE ICE
characterContinuityAssessment.reason: The chapter materially advances the recovery operation and consumes equipment but does not change the established recurring cast's durable personal knowledge, relationships, injuries, obligations, skills, or long-term plans. Broussard applies already-established survival-focused command competence, Jalesthesian continues established cooperative observation, Kelm continues ship-preservation command, and Sella continues established technical recovery work. The equipment/perimeter consequences are persisted in the circuit rather than manufacturing redundant personal-state entries.

active.title: House Vallimere’s Sons
active.currentEndpoint: Continuation IV — The First Appeal. Eleven days into the one-term assessment pilot, Cadet Commander Solren appeals a failed evaluation after abandoning a damaged troop transport to preserve a refinery and inhabited moon. The review establishes that evaluators must distinguish hindsight disagreement with a command choice from a demonstrated defect in the reasoning available when the order was issued. House Caldrake has a personal stake through a dead officer aboard the transport, but the appeal is resolved procedurally rather than by duel or political capitulation. The Academy codifies the distinction and the pilot continues.
active.nextSlice: On the next House Vallimere rotation, let the one-term pilot generate a new consequence rather than another restatement of the review-board philosophy. Preserve the new appeal precedent: instructor hindsight or moral preference alone is not proof of defective command reasoning. Solren's case remains an institutional example, not an excuse to turn every future chapter into courtroom procedure. Continue the trio's development as teachers and preserve Darcelle's increasing confidence when technical/procedural ground is firm, Renault's restrained humor, Prite's reluctance to reduce doctrine to slogans, the Headmaster's institutional protection, and Vane's Priority Omega role. Shared history should shorten dialogue.

active.title: Matron Lagas Atrovald
active.currentEndpoint: Continuation III — The Record That Waited. Atrovald's S-Rank search finds a possible Witness Two in Mortuary-Seventeen: a sealed remains container whose destruction record says the textual witness was burned, whose mass still matches the ancient certificate, and whose hidden physical inscription says not to destroy it until the first is present. Predulum, without being shown that inscription, reports a fragmentary memory of a furnace, ash and the phrase 'Wait until the first is present.' The missing fifty-third guard acquires a paper-only identity, Custody Auxiliar Hesk Venn, plus an unsigned tomorrow-dated instruction returning him to Null-Seven. Atrovald refuses to sign it and orders future-dated authority treated as evidence rather than instruction.
active.nextSlice: On the next Atrovald rotation, advance the search for Hesk Venn and the provenance of the possible Witness Two without opening or reconciling evidence merely for explanatory convenience. Preserve Predulum's independent furnace/phrase memory, Atrovald's rule that future-dated orders are evidence until issued in ordinary sequence, the unopened Mortuary-Seventeen container, the 53/52 custody discrepancy, Witness Four and Predulum still sealed in Null-Seven, and the unresolved tomorrow-dated accession. Do not explain the anomaly as generic Warp/daemon mechanics. Apply natural-conversation governance: shared facts should shape decisions and shorthand, not be re-recited.

active.title: On the Fuzzy Edge
active.currentEndpoint: Continuation III — Lower Ossuary Nineteen. Javard follows the seventeen-year-pending Ephram Sol transfer through the cathedral underworks. The supposedly sump-condemned route includes a dry containment wall and leads to a clean, apparently occupied niche labeled EPHRAM SOL despite the transfer remaining administratively pending. Ossuary Maintenance Six has stamped annual transfer-readiness inspections on the same liturgical vigil for seventeen years. Javard deliberately leaves the niche unopened. Caldris then reports that the recovering Pontiff Montpclair asked by name whether Interrogator Javard had 'opened Sol,' although Javard never completed his intended introduction. Archive Servitor Nine reacts to Sol by printing 'DO NOT OPEN UNTIL HE ASKS.' Javard chooses to interview Montpclair before disturbing the niche.
active.nextSlice: On the next On the Fuzzy Edge rotation, continue with Javard's interview of the recovering Pontiff Montpclair. Preserve that Sol's niche remains unopened, the old Inquisitorial archive seal remains intact, the Tides of Tomorrow return/register contradiction remains unresolved, Vorn's Graveheart evidence and disputed-reader mark remain live, and neither Javard nor the reader has earned an explanation for who 'he' is or what 'open Sol' ultimately means. Montpclair knows Javard's name and asked whether he had opened Sol before being briefed on the ossuary descent; establish how he knows only through evidence and bounded conversation, not an exposition dump. Maintain Javard's patient procedural method and dry wit as an accent.

active.title: Of Blood and Wires: The Litanies of Tenelja Station
active.currentEndpoint: Source story complete: Sister Arbentia finishes another Tenelja Station medicae shift after helping keep a catastrophically void-burned Xanadu Salvage Company patient alive. She remains a low-ranking healer caught between Sister Bethany's devotional medicine and Magos Biologis-Abstrator Abraxas 8207's mechanistic practice, hopes to see her intermittent lover Rix on the following day, and remains denied access to the scriptorum archives despite being judged capable because the station has no bureaucratic need for her advancement.
active.nextSlice: Begin the continuation with the promised next-day meeting with Rix and let the surviving Xanadu patient's accident become a practical medicae/salvage consequence rather than an instant conspiracy reveal. Establish what Rix knows, what Arbentia wants from study, and what Tenelja routinely fails to provide before escalating the station's medical and infrastructure pressures.

allowedInstitutions: local medicae order / Silent Daughters of Penance and Balm
eraLock.forbiddenDrift: Do not import famous canon characters, galaxy-level stakes, or unsupported later-history knowledge. Keep Tenelja's pressures local, institutional, medical, industrial and human unless the story itself earns a wider connection.

fullArcAuthority.finalState: The Tenelja arc ends after Arbentia has crossed from competent invisible labor into recognized medical responsibility during a station-scale casualty crisis, with her access to advanced study materially changed and her relationship with Rix forced into an explicit durable form. Tenelja itself survives damaged rather than being conveniently destroyed or transformed, Bethany and Abraxas remain functioning professionals whose opposed doctrines have both been tested, and the reader understands which failures were ordinary institutional decay and which were preventable human choices.
fullArcAuthority.completionBoundary: End the book once the acute casualty crisis is resolved, the surviving wards and infrastructure are stable enough to return to ordinary Tenelja misery, responsibility for the preventable failures has propagated into station procedure, Arbentia's study/status question has received a concrete answer, and Arbentia and Rix have made a choice about what they are to each other. Later station incidents belong to a new story, not Chapter 19 by inertia.

targetBudget.sourceEquivalent: Source story functions as Chapters 1-3 of the arc; continuation should normally close within roughly 15 additional chapters.

macroArcs.name: Blood and Wires
macroArcs.purpose: Source baseline: establish Tenelja's medical culture, Bethany/Abraxas doctrinal friction, Arbentia's invisible competence, the void-burned Xanadu survivor, Rix, and the locked scriptorum.

macroArcs.name: What Survives the Shift
macroArcs.purpose: Pay the promised Rix meeting; follow the Xanadu injury into salvage-work consequences; show Arbentia seeking knowledge she is denied while recurring station failures make that denial increasingly costly.

macroArcs.name: The Cost of Necessary Ignorance
macroArcs.purpose: A cluster of industrial/void casualties stresses Tenelja. Arbentia's accumulated observations matter operationally. Bethany and Abraxas must each be right about different parts of treatment, forcing cooperation rather than a winner-takes-all theology debate.

macroArcs.name: Triage of a Dying Station
macroArcs.purpose: A station-system failure converts chronic decay into an acute casualty crisis. Arbentia receives responsibility because competence and scarcity leave no cleaner option. Rix's salvage knowledge and access become useful but expose him to real cost.

macroArcs.name: After the Alarms
macroArcs.purpose: Resolve the wards, accountability, study access and Arbentia/Rix relationship. Show changed procedure and ordinary work resuming; close before a fresh mystery or catastrophe can restart the plot.

irreversibleBeats: Arbentia and Rix meet as promised, converting the source's private hope into an on-page relationship baseline.
A preventable medical or infrastructure failure occurs because useful knowledge is institutionally rationed or jurisdictionally trapped; it cannot be blamed on generic stupidity.
Bethany and Abraxas are forced to rely on one another's method in a case neither doctrine can solve alone, permanently changing how their arguments function without making either abandon belief.
Arbentia acts beyond her nominal station during the casualty crisis and becomes accountable for the outcome; she cannot return to being wholly invisible afterward.
Rix chooses whether to risk livelihood, salvage standing or bodily safety to help Arbentia/the ward; the relationship gains a cost rather than remaining an off-shift comfort.
The crisis leaves Tenelja with a concrete procedural or resource consequence that remains after the patients stop screaming.

characterTrajectories.Arbentia: Invisible competent nurse -> frustrated would-be scholar -> practitioner whose denied learning becomes an operational problem -> reluctant decision-maker under casualty pressure -> recognized responsibility with a concrete answer about further study. Do not turn competence into sudden genius or sainthood.
characterTrajectories.Rix: Pleasurable off-shift connection and salvage contact -> source of specific practical knowledge and competing obligations -> person who must choose what Arbentia and Tenelja are worth risking -> durable relationship outcome, whether committed, bounded or ended. Do not reduce him to rescue muscle.
characterTrajectories.Bethany: Confident devotional healer -> confronted by cases where conviction cannot substitute for mechanism -> learns to cooperate without surrendering faith. Her compassion and institutional rigidity must both remain real.
characterTrajectories.Abraxas8207: Mechanistic solver -> confronted by cases where optimization cannot account for consent, morale, faith or human endurance -> adapts practice without becoming sentimental or renouncing Mechanicus logic.
characterTrajectories.XanaduSurvivor: Evidence that survival creates debts, paperwork and downstream consequences; may connect medicae and salvage threads, but must not become a convenient secret villain or exposition device.

seedPayoffObligations.payoff: Carry medical debt, work incapacity, salvage-company consequences or testimony forward; survival must have aftermath.

seedPayoffObligations.payoff: Escalate from argument-as-routine to forced complementary practice under pressure.

seedPayoffObligations.seed: Tenelja's flickering lights, gravity whine, rust and decaying systems.
seedPayoffObligations.payoff: At least one acute failure must grow from previously visible maintenance reality, with causal warning signs rather than a surprise disaster.

seedPayoffObligations.payoff: Use ordinary private life as something crisis threatens and as a measure of what survival preserves; do not treat domestic texture as disposable filler.

continuityControls: Reader knowledge and character knowledge remain separate; Arbentia begins with no hidden explanation for the Xanadu accident beyond what her role exposes.
Tenelja's dysfunction must arise from maintenance debt, resource rationing, jurisdiction, doctrine, staffing and incentives rather than everyone becoming incompetent.
Do not convert the source's local medical/station-life scale into a daemon, xenos, Inquisitorial or galaxy-saving plot without a separately authorized later arc.
Deaths and injuries consume named expertise, relationships, supplies, beds, time and morale; casualties are not grimdark decoration.
Shared knowledge shortens dialogue. Bethany, Abraxas and Arbentia do not repeatedly explain their own established doctrines or jobs to one another.
The source story remains canonical baseline prose; architecture governs continuation and must not rewrite its events.
installmentMap: 4: Rix meeting; Xanadu survivor aftermath; define what Arbentia knows and wants.
5: Scriptorum petition consequence and a routine case where missing knowledge costs time.
6: Salvage-side visit or evidence grounds Tenelja's maintenance economy and Rix's obligations.
7: First preventable near-miss ties medical and infrastructure jurisdictions together.
8: Casualty influx begins; Bethany and Abraxas disagree for materially different reasons.
9: Arbentia identifies a pattern but lacks authority/resources to act cleanly.
10: A treatment succeeds only through combined doctrinal/mechanical practice.
11: Administrative response protects throughput before learning; consequences accumulate.
12: Rix faces a salvage-company conflict that makes helping Arbentia costly.
13: Seeded station-system weakness fails under load and creates the main casualty event.
14: Arbentia is forced into responsibility beyond nominal rank.
15: Rix's practical access/knowledge matters; Bethany and Abraxas divide work intelligently.
16: Crisis peak and irreversible choice; stabilize the station without miraculous repair.
17: Accountability, ward aftermath, losses and procedural changes.
18: Resolve study/status and Arbentia/Rix; return Tenelja to changed ordinary life and end.
